_source: A Night Off design doc pp. 17-18 (Bar games: where, players, how it plays, what drink does, stakes and stories) and p. 30 (--game-check: a bot against each hustler at 0, 40 and 80 drunk; targets sober 55%, drunk 35%, wrecked 10%). Skills multiply the thrower's error: lower is better; a sober player is 1.0. The aim curve is the meter's effect on everyone's error (Merry is steadier: the courage bonus).

opponents.name: Red Haddock
opponents.tell: Throws left-handed when nervous: watch his hands before the big dart

opponents.name: Captain Vane
opponents.tell: Shouts before he throws; a bad loser

opponents.name: the bartender
opponents.tell: Plays one game a night, for your tab

opponents.name: Sly Pennick
opponents.tell: Scratches his ear before a bluff; misses the first game on purpose

opponents.name: Bosun Grieve
opponents.tell: Teaches pool for a pint; talks you through the shot

golf.where: the yard, nine holes (closes at 2 a.m.)

opponents.name: Finnegan
opponents.tell: Whistles before he nudges his ball

slots._weights: per reel, in symbol order; machine 2 is the honest one (the bartender knows which)

fortune._deck: The fortune deck, 22 cards (doc p. 42). A reading is three: who you'll meet, what you'll do, how it ends; generated from the night's real schedule, so it's true. A second reading is a lie she tells for fun.
lies: A tall stranger will buy you a drink and ask nothing in return.
The slot machines are all honest tonight.
The bartender is secretly fond of you.
A whale will come in at midnight. Be kind to it.
Your luck at darts is the best it will ever be.
The goat is your friend. Trust the goat.
You will be home by ten.
